meta.hazardAnalysis:
- Ergonomics: Potential for musculoskeletal strain due to prolonged computer use, improper workstation setup, and repetitive data entry tasks.

- Trips, Slips, & Falls: Risk of injury from unorganized office supplies, loose electrical/network cabling, and wet floors in common transition areas.

- Electrical Safety: Potential for fire or shock from overloaded power strips, daisy-chained extension cords, and damaged office equipment wiring.

- Physical Environment: Risks associated with improper manual lifting of heavy office files or equipment and the use of non-industrial step stools.

- Emergency Egress: Potential for delayed evacuation if hallways, fire exits, or electrical panels are blocked by stored administrative materials.
meta.riskManagementNotes:
🛑 Hazard Identification & Reporting
Your Responsibility: Mishap prevention relies on you identifying, reporting, and correcting hazards immediately.

Guidelines for Personnel:

- How to Report: Report any hazardous conditions placing people or property at risk to your Supervisor, Facility Manager, Unit Safety Representative (USR), or Safety Office.

- Reporting Tools: Use DAF Form 457 (Hazard Report) or the SAFEREP electronic system.

- Your Protections:  You can report anonymously. Supervisors/Managers are strictly prohibited from reprisal, coercion, or discrimination against anyone reporting a safety hazard.

- Near Misses: Report near misses. They are leading indicators of future mishaps involving manpower, equipment, environment, or methods.
 
🛡️ Control Selection & Hazard Abatement: When a hazard cannot be fixed on the spot, leadership uses a systemic approach to prioritize and control the risk.

Risk Assessment Codes (RAC): Hazards are assigned a RAC by the safety office to prioritize how quickly they must be abated.

How We Control Hazards:

- Engineering/Planning: The preferred method is to engineer the hazard out completely (e.g., redesigning the workspace or equipment).

- Procedural Actions: If it cannot be engineered out, we implement procedures to minimize risk (e.g., mandatory PPE, operational limits, or frequent inspections).

- Interim Controls: Temporary safety measures put in place while waiting for a permanent fix. You must strictly follow all interim controls.

- Imminent Danger: If a situation is critical or presents imminent danger, STOP OPERATIONS immediately and withdraw personnel. Notify the commander or supervisor in charge right away. Work cannot resume until the hazard is mitigated or risk is formally accepted by the appropriate commander.

🔄 Daily Risk Management (RM): RM is Everyone's Job: Commanders mandate RM use at all levels, but personal accountability falls on the individual executing the job.

- Constantly Reevaluate: If anything about your job changes (weather, equipment status, personnel changes, new procedures), you must reevaluate the risk and adjust your controls before continuing.

- Risk Decision Escalation: Accountability is a critically important area of RM. The accountable person is the one who makes the decision (approves the control measures), and hence, the right person, at the appropriate level, must make the decision. The following risk acceptance authority levels are established for all deliberate RM assessments IAW AFI 90-802, paragraph 2.9.3.2.

−Extremely High and High = Wing CC
−Medium = Group CC/CV
−Low = Squadron CC/CV or Staff Agency Director

These risk acceptance authority levels are not applicable to formal test operations or acquisition/system safety. Other guidance assigns these authority levels.

Training: 
- RM Fundamentals: Mandatory initial course on myLearning IAW DAFI 91-802, Para 4.1.1, covering DAF RM processes for on/off-duty situations.

- RM Refresher (ART): Mandatory annual training IAW DAFI 91-802, Para 4.1.4, to reinforce RM proficiency and ensure continuous safety awareness. Training materials that support RM ART including PowerPoint slides, and exercise example scenarios are available on the AFSEC Risk Management AF Portal site. 

- Training Repository	: Wing Safety maintains training materials, briefings and examples on their SharePoint site and AFSEC Risk Management AF Portal site.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
As a collateral organization on Camp Murray, a joint base under WMD authority, the 194th Wing will support and adhere to all installation, DAF and ANG policies.

NOTE:  Motorcycle Riders in Military Status: DSGs - The MUSTT requirement applies when they are in a military status (e.g., during Unit Training Assemblies [UTAs] or active-duty periods). However, units may track DSG riders even outside drill periods to ensure compliance year-round, especially given the Air Force’s emphasis on reducing motorcycle mishaps (e.g., seven airmen fatalities from October 2022 to January 2023, three without proper training).

Local Traffic & Driving Hazards: 

Winter Driving (October - April):

Rain & Hydroplaning: Persistent heavy rain increases stopping distances and hydroplaning risk (especially in I-5 ruts). Mitigation: Reduce speed.

Black Ice & Frost: The "freeze-thaw" cycle creates invisible black ice, particularly during early morning commutes. High Risk Areas: Bridges, overpasses, and shaded roads.

Fog & Low Visibility: Dense morning fog requires the use of low-beam headlights only.

Snow Disruptions: Even minor snow (1-3 inches) causes major gridlock due to limited clearing equipment and driver inexperience. Mitigation: Utilize telework or alternate plans if forecasted.

Mountain Passes: Snoqualmie/Stevens Passes experience severe winter conditions separate from the lowlands. Mandatory: WSDOT compliance and traction chains.

Interstate 5 Corridor (DuPont / JBLM / Tacoma):

Extreme Congestion: Severe stop-and-go traffic is common, especially during peak commute hours (0600-0900 / 1500-1800) and near JBLM gates.

Choke Points: Anticipate major delays and merging hazards near the Tacoma Dome, Puyallup River Bridge, and the "Fife Curve."

High Mishap Risk: High traffic volume and constant construction/lane shifts lead to frequent rear-end collisions.

Deceptive Hazards & Wildlife:

Sun Glare: Low-angle sun on wet roads causes blinding glare; polarized sunglasses are highly recommended.

Wildlife (Deer): High risk of deer strikes on rural/suburban routes, especially during dawn and dusk.

Rural & Residential Roads:

Slow Vehicles: Expect farm equipment on State Routes (e.g., SR 7, 507, 410). Pass only when legal and safe.

Lower Priority Clearing: Rural and residential roads are low priority for snow/ice removal and may remain hazardous long after highways are clear.

Speed vs. Conditions: Posted limits (up to 60 mph) may not be safe during adverse weather.

There is not an emergency medical treatment facility located on Camp Murray. The nearest Emergency medical facility is located on JBLM at the Madigan Army Medical Center. If emergency responders are needed, call 911 from any base telephone. (Note: If you dial 911 from your cell phone, it may delay response since the call goes to an off-base responder). The Fire Department will respond with paramedics/EMTs that are on shift. They can evaluate the injuries and recommend further medical attention. If further medical attention is needed, an ambulance may be called to transport the individual to a medical facility. If it is not a severe injury, but the person feels that a doctor needs to check it, they may go to an off-base medical provider of their choice within a reasonable distance (25 miles).

meta.documentationNotes:
Documentation And Maintenance:

Training can be logged as a single entry. Direct the employee to log into Percipio and complete the ANG - Job Safety Training Outline Review. This fulfills the baseline requirement. https://usaf.percipio.com/linked-contents/e86851b1-2dfe-4732-88cb-3a2daaa91ea3/landing.  

Training Record: Supervisors will document all safety, fire, and health training using AF Form 55, Employee Safety and Health Record, or an equivalent electronic system (e.g., a printout from ARCNET, or a local digital record).

Note: If the AF Form 55 is mandated for use as the training documentation device, the entity that mandated the form usage will prescribe the requirement in writing to include entries that require signatures, e.g., HAZCOM, respirator, low powered industrial, hazardous energy control (LOTO), fall protection, confined spaces, radiation safety, laser safety, etc.

Refresher Training: 

• Will be conducted and documented when employees demonstrate a lack of understanding of their required safety responsibilities or, 
• If training has a specified frequency for recurrence (e.g. such as is called for in DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 21, Hazardous Energy Control).


Disposition: When an individual permanently changes station (PCS), separates, or retires, the supervisor or Unit Training Manager (UTM) will provide them with a copy of their completed training record to hand-carry. The unit will destroy its copy one year after the member's departure.

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: Common local training item often broken out separately with fixed and portable ladder rules
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use local ladder lesson plans, manufacturer instructions, and AF walking-working surface guidance. OSHA 2254 (2015 edition) does not provide a dedicated general-industry ladder training summary in the same way it does for lockout, forklifts, or confined spaces, so this remains primarily AF/local-driven.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Personnel using ladders at any working height must be trained when first assigned, and that training must include hands-on instruction covering ladder defects, electrocution hazards, positioning, and placement for various job sites. Training must be documented under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 7.4.3.7
selectedModules.notes:
Frequency: Annual

Regulation: 91-203. 29 CFR 1910.23

Description: Critical Safety; This course is conducted at local level. Personnel who use ladders at working heights of six feet or more will be adequately trained in the care and use of different types of ladders.  Training will be conducted IAW 29 CFR 1910.23.  The supervisor, or a designated trainer, will conduct this training when a worker is first assigned and periodically as needed.  Wing Safety will provide training and presentation materials. This course covers hands-on instruction on the safe use of ladders.  To include: inspection of ladders for defects, possible electrocution hazards, and proper positioning and placement of ladders for various job sites.  It is provided by the supervisor or a designated trainer and is mandatory for all individuals who utilize a ladder.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Local emergency response briefing and lockdown procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Tie this to the local emergency action plan, shelter/lockdown locations, notification methods, and commander-directed response procedures.
selectedModules.notes:
Active Shooter: Annual training via Percipio covering "Avoid, Deny, Defend" principles, with local procedures directing personnel to barricade in place or evacuate to the Bldg. 81 (PCRC) rally point for accountability.

Local Hazards: Potential for workplace violence or active shooter incidents within Wing Staff facilities (Bldgs. 50, 51, 54, and 109).
Local Procedures: Execute "Avoid, Deny, Defend." Evacuate if possible or barricade in a secure area away from windows. Once safe or when officially cleared by Law Enforcement, proceed to the primary rally point at Bldg. 81 (PCRC) for accountability.
Training Summary: Mandatory course preparing personnel to identify active shooter characteristics, understand "Avoid-Deny-Defend" principles, and learn appropriate actions to take during an attack and when law enforcement arrives.
Training Location: Completed via DAF E-Learning (Percipio): https://share.percipio.com/cd/VzXuGtFNX
Interval / Documentation: Annual requirement. Completion records are automatically maintained within the Percipio learning management system.

selectedModules.title: Office Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chpter 2.
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
Frequency: One Time

Regulation: DAFMAN 91-203

Description: Non-Critical Safety; This course is conducted at local level. Employers are required to provide an office environment free from hazards. Management should ensure that employees are educated about the many office hazards which many workers may not be aware of, such as noise, poor ergonomics, damaged electrical wires, inoperative fire extinguishers, and lack of emergency plans. Personnel assigned to office work environments are required to complete office safety training.  Supervisors can be provided training when personnel assigned.

Records are maintained in Percipio.

selectedModules.title: Job Safety Training Outline Review
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 91-202 - The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Mishap Prevention Program Chapter 14
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
Training on the mandatory core items of the JSTO can be documented as a single consolidated entry (e.g., using a single course code for JSTO mandatory training), whereas job-specific items and any training identified in a Bioenvironmental Engineering (BE) survey must be documented individually. 

-Authorized methods for this documentation include the AF Form 55 (Employee Safety and Health Record), electronic tracking systems like AFFORMs, MAF LOG C2, or G081, or other locally developed products, provided they capture the minimum required data: the trainee's full name, the type of training, and the date completed. 

Note: Nther the trainer's nor the trainee's signature is required for this documentation unless it is specifically mandated in writing by the applicable chain of authority for high-risk programs such as lockout/tagout, fall protection, or HAZCOM.
